title: Total Orders per Customer
description:
Count how many orders each customer has placed. Return the customer id and their order count.

**Table: orders**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| customer_id | INT |
| order_date | DATE |
| status | VARCHAR |
| total_amount | DECIMAL |

Output columns: `customer_id`, `order_count`. Order by `order_count` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 1, DATE '2026-01-05', 'completed', 100.00), (2, 2, DATE '2026-01-06', 'completed', 75.50), (3, 1, DATE '2026-01-07', 'pending', 150.00), (4, 3, DATE '2026-01-08', 'completed', 200.00), (5, 1, DATE '2026-01-09', 'completed', 90.00), (6, 2, DATE '2026-01-10', 'completed', 60.00);
solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY order_count DESC

test_cases.description: Customer 1 has 3, customer 2 has 2, customer 3 has 1

hints: GROUP BY customer_id groups all orders for the same customer together.
COUNT(*) counts the number of rows (orders) in each group.
explanation: Grouping by `customer_id` creates one row per customer. `COUNT(*)` tells us how many orders each customer placed. Customer 1 placed 3 orders (ids 1, 3, 5), customer 2 placed 2 (ids 2, 6), customer 3 placed 1 (id 4).
